Title: Changing the card text template to make entry easier

Messages.Author: the1andonlime
Messages.Body:
So I have been going on about modifying the card text templates to reduce the barrier to entry for a while now (generally falls to death ears on the old google groups) and since  Ankha was talking about simplified cards for new players , I thought I would bring the topic up again.

Held a demo game recently for a couple of friends and the main feedback I got was that the cards had too many keywords that were not explained, making it difficult to learn the cards while learning the rules at the same time.

I propose (as I have, time and again) to put simple little explanation of certain keywords on the cards themselves. Specifically on crypt cards (because, while I like the way Ankha puts explanation text for action modifiers, political action cards, etc, I think space may be an issue).

Really, how hard can it be to put "(title, x votes)" next to every bishop, primogen, magaji or cardinal and "(unique title, x votes) next to every prince, archbishop, justicar, inner circle or regent? Of course all these will only appear on new cards or reprints.

This immediately makes a few things easier:
1. Cards that require titled vampires (those that say "Require a titled vampire" or "Only usable by a titled vampire") or require a non-titled vampire no longer require explanation beyond "RTFC"
2. The number of votes each vampire generates becomes immediately obvious
3. Titles that are unique are also immediately identifiable

I think, with all the talk of bringing in new players, this is a good step for the future and now is a good time to start.

Messages.Author: direwolf
Messages.Body:
Don't expect this to happen. In V:tES players expect their opponents to recognize every card they play just by announcing the name of the card as it is played.

When we say "Muaziz bleeds with govern" it's expected that you know govern = "Govern the Unaligned," which is a bleed action at +2 bleed, and Muaziz has +1 stealth.

In reality, you are supposed to announce "Muaziz bleeds with Govern the Unaligned for 3 at +1 stealth."

Players are expected to know how many votes each title grants. And VEKN is so afraid of making changes to cards already printed, they will never change the format of a card to include more information.

Common sense changes like you propose won't happen. Vampires don't change and change is bad.

Independent Futurist. Contrarian (titled, X votes where X is the number of votes as the acting minion.) Target Vitals is always the better combat card.

I suppose you have the "title (x votes)" in mind.
Adding the number of votes after the title has nothing to do with intuitiveness because either the player have read the section about referendum and knows what title and votes are about, or he hasn't and the concept of # votes won't help him.
Adding the number of votes is more a help for beginners which is welcome on initiation sets (that's why I added them on my  demo cards -- and you can see that there's a lot of text as soon as you begin to add rules reminders) but becomes quickly redundant and space-wasting when you've played a few games.

I don't think you can make standard VTES cards "intuitive". If you haven't read the rules, you won't get far.

If you have a look on Magic cards, only core sets have reminders about keywords such as Flying and so on. The volume of cards printed and expansions, as well as the quantity of vanilla cards (1/1 flying creature with no text) make it easy to add reminder text. Classical sets don't have reminder (except for new keywords, which doesn't happen frequently in VTES).

To cut a long story short, I think that "Prince of Miami" is perfectly clear and doesn't need any additional reminder text. It's more useful either to design a beginner's set with special cards, and/or a set of reminders cards (the existing ones have to many informations on them): one with the titles and what they're worth and how a political action works, one for combat, one with the turn layout, etc.

In fact, playing on the  playmat should be enough. The number of votes a Prince has is written on it.

If people have ideas to make the game more "intuitive", please share!

Prince of Paris, France

Messages.Author: the1andonlime
Messages.Body:
See, I believe that, ideally, potential players can pick up vtes without going "WTF?! TL;DR, not going to play something so complicated". I am specifically talking about those who have no access to an existing playgroup to show them the ropes.

I agree that too much reminder text for keywords do make the text overly long, but there are too many players (potential and existing) who keep asking how many votes certain titles have.

Would you agree that, after quickly reading through the rules, a player should be able to jump into the game without having to constantly reference rules or reminder cards?

That said, I concur that if we do get a chance to do beginner sets (which can be used with existing cards) on a more or less regular basis, that would be the best place to have cards with reminder text.

However, without such a set anytime in the horizon, I still think my proposal will help the game.

Messages.Author: direwolf
Messages.Body:
This game is around 17 years old?

Card layouts have changed somewhat in that time. A crypt card in vampire takes up about 60.5%* of the usable surface of a card (compared to a Magic: the Gathering card which the image takes up 42.6%)

The reason is that the portraits are in an elliptical frame, and the outer corners are not utilized for card function. The AREA of the ellipse is about the same as the area of a magic card image.

You want to put more information on a vampire without crowding the text? Find a way to use that space.
